comments.author: Rashid
comments.body:
Try to intercept your opponent and melee with your broadside against opponent's bow; ---> At the end of melee you are blocking opponent's path and hopefully your teammate would anchor behind the opponent's stern threatening a critical hit, both of which forces the opponent to turn; ---> Most people assume you will continue to move forward while laying mines as you pass so your opponent is likely to turn to the other side; ---> Predicting that you turn that side and lay sime mines right after melee ends;

comments.author: Edgedemon
comments.body:
complex question Slideman.
if you get Roaring Sea Mines, Moored Mines or Special sea mine this skill can be a total game changer, but compared to what a bow crit could do their damage will never be high, so you need to be able to outrun your target and avoid crits which makes it hard to use effectively.

comments.author: Caddy
comments.body: This is more of a support skill in my mind. Like Edgedemon mentioned, even with r20 minelaying, it's not gonna damage >1k. However, mines take significant dura off ship parts and ships, and it used to be a common tactic for folks to use a r15 minelaying job to beat up ship parts/max dura of their enemies. That coupled with some of the mine skills can make this seriously deadly for PvP, and also RSM can greatly help in PvE as well vs. say a strong ganador or the admiral of a strong quest fleet.
